questions.question_text: Mechanism of action of buprenorphine is via partial agonism at?
questions.explanation: Buprenorphine is a partial opiate agonist at mu receptors.

questions.question_text: How much Zuclopenthixol depot is equivalent to 50mg of haloperidol given every four weeks?
questions.explanation: 200mg / 2 weeks or 400mg/4 weeks of zuclopenthixol depot is equivalent to 50mg of haloperidol depot every 4 weeks.

questions.question_text: A 27-year-old man who is taking mirtazapine for generalized anxiety disorder and major depression experiences significant sedation at a dosage of 7.5 mg/day. Which neurotransmitter receptor is most likely being affected?
questions.explanation: Blockade of 5HT2 receptors by mirtazapine helps improving the quality of sleep in depressed patients.

questions.question_text: Buspirone acts on?
questions.explanation: Buspirone acts on 5HT1­a receptors. It is a partial agonist at post-synaptic 5HT1­a receptors.

questions.question_text: Weight gain caused by clozapine is possibly related to?
questions.explanation: The mechanism of weight gain during treatment with antipsychotics is poorly understood, but antagonism of serotonin 5­HT2C receptors has been implicated.

questions.question_text: A 85-year-old lady presents with moderately severe agitated depression. The most appropriate intervention is?

options.text: Trial of sertraline after stopping venlafaxine

questions.explanation: Mirtazapine works well in combination with venlafaxine; it will be the ideal choice in the above scenario.

questions.question_text: Which of the following types of drug molecules mimic endogenous chemical transmission?
questions.explanation: Agonists are drugs that mimic endogenous transmission.

questions.question_text: Disulfiram acts on?
questions.explanation: In usual doses, disulfiram acts via inhibition of acetaldehyde dehydrogenase.

questions.question_text: Which of the following actions can cause anorgasmia?
questions.explanation: Alpha 1 antagonism can cause anorgasmia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following has atypical antipsychotic activity?
questions.explanation: Amisulpride has atypical antipsychotic activity.

questions.question_text: Drug that is comparatively safe as an adjunctive to MAOI in treating depression is?
questions.explanation: MAOIs potentiate the actions of TCAs, which may provide an explanation for the use of such a combination in the treatment of therapy-resistant depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a partial D2 agonist?
questions.explanation: Aripiprazole is a dopamine D2 receptor partial agonist.

questions.question_text: The therapeutic effects of conventional antipsychotics is mainly due to?

options.text: Blockade of dopamine­2 receptors in the nigrostriatal pathway
Blockade of dopamine­2 receptors in the mesocortical pathway
Blockade of dopamine­2 receptors in the tuberoinfundibular pathway
Blockade of dopamine­2 receptors in the mesolimbic pathway

correct_answer.text: Blockade of dopamine­2 receptors in the mesolimbic pathway

correct_answers.text: Blockade of dopamine­2 receptors in the mesolimbic pathway

questions.explanation: Blockade of dopamine­2 receptors in the mesolimbic pathway leads to the therapeutic effects.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a 5HT1A partial agonist?
questions.explanation: Buspirone's mechanism of action is related to 5HT partial agonism.

questions.question_text: Tyramine gains neuronal access and releases stored catecholamines via which of the following routes?
questions.explanation: Tyramine enters the presynaptic neuron through amine uptake pumps that are blocked by antidepressants.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following is a weak inhibitor of cytochrome P450?
questions.explanation: Citalopram does not produce significant cytochrome P450 inhibition and is considered the safest.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following has a stimulant effect?
questions.explanation: Desipramine has relative selectivity for noradrenaline reuptake and has a stimulant effect.

questions.question_text: A patient on mirtazapine treatment develops rapidly spreading bacterial infection. Which of the following must be immediately checked?
questions.explanation: Severe neutropenia is a potential life-threatening side effect of mirtazapine, and checking differential count is crucial.

questions.question_text: The chronic administration of tricyclics results in?

options.text: Down regulation of beta and alpha adrenergic receptors

questions.explanation: Chronic administration of antidepressant drugs causes a downregulation of beta receptors.

questions.question_text: A new drug A is a non­competitive antagonist at NMDA receptors. If availability of glutamate at the receptor sites is increased experimentally after administering drug A, which of the following can happen?

options.text: Effect of drug A is partially reversed
Effect of drug A is reversed fully

correct_answer.text: Effect of drug A is partially reversed

correct_answers.text: Effect of drug A is partially reversed

questions.explanation: Noncompetitive antagonists reduce both the potency and efficacy of agonists, so their effects can only be partially reversed.

questions.question_text: Endogenous substrates for monoamine oxidase (MAO) isoenzymes include?
questions.explanation: Endogenous monoamines serotonin, dopamine, and norepinephrine are broken down by MAO enzymes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following medications has been found to be effective in patients with premature ejaculation?
questions.explanation: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) are useful in the treatment of premature ejaculation.

questions.question_text: The drug alprazolam acts on?
questions.explanation: Alprazolam is a benzodiazepine; it acts via GABA mechanisms.

questions.question_text: The mechanism of action for Sodium valproate?
questions.explanation: Valproate acts on the activity of histone deacetylase and increases GABA levels.

questions.question_text: The pharmacological activity of benzodiazepines depends on its action on which of the following receptors?
questions.explanation: Benzodiazepines act on GABA­a receptor complex and potentiate GABAergic function.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following has antiepileptic activity?
questions.explanation: Gabapentin is known for its antiepileptic properties.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antidementia drugs acts directly on nicotine receptors?
questions.explanation: Galantamine is derived from alkaloids and acts as an agonist at nicotinic receptor sites.

questions.question_text: Mechanism of action of acamprosate is?
questions.explanation: Acamprosate is thought to involve interference with excitatory amino acids such as glutamate.

questions.question_text: The mechanism of action of cyproheptadine is?
questions.explanation: Cyproheptadine is a sedating antihistamine that acts by blocking H1 receptors.

questions.question_text: The mechanism of action of barbiturates is by?

options.text: Increasing the number of chloride channels
Increasing the duration of chloride channel opening
Increasing the frequency of chloride channels opening

correct_answer.text: Increasing the duration of chloride channel opening

correct_answers.text: Increasing the duration of chloride channel opening

questions.explanation: Barbiturates serve to increase the duration of chloride channel opening.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements best describes the receptor profile of trazodone?

options.text: It is a serotonin, dopamine and norepinephrine agonist
It is a serotonin, dopamine and norepinephrine antagonist
It is a mixed serotonin antagonist/agonist.

correct_answer.text: It is a mixed serotonin antagonist/agonist.

correct_answers.text: It is a mixed serotonin antagonist/agonist.

questions.explanation: Trazodone's most potent binding property is 5-HT2A antagonism; at higher doses, it acts as a SERT blocker.

questions.question_text: Which of the following street drugs is called a dissociative anaesthetic?
questions.explanation: Ketamine is known for producing a state of dissociative anaesthesia.

questions.question_text: The enzyme/s that metabolise/s most of the body dopamine:
questions.explanation: Dopamine is metabolized by MAO and COMT in liver, kidney, and plasma.

questions.question_text: Excitotoxicity that is secondary to glutamatergic overstimulation results in neuronal damage. This is the basis of treating patients with neurodegenerative disorders with which of the following medications?
questions.explanation: Memantine is a noncompetitive NMDA antagonist considered neuroprotective in treating neurodegenerative disorders.

questions.question_text: Which drug acts as a full agonist at Mu receptor and has a long half-life?
questions.explanation: Methadone is a full mu opioid agonist with a half-life of approximately 24 hours.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following has been postulated as the pharmacological basis of clozapine related hypersalivation?
questions.explanation: Clozapine is associated with hypersalivation, potentially due to M4 agonism.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following is the least sedative of tricyclic antidepressants?
questions.explanation: Nortriptyline is considered the least sedative tricyclic antidepressant.

questions.question_text: The mechanism of action of varenicline tartrate is?
questions.explanation: Varenicline is a nicotinic acetylcholine receptor partial agonist that relieves withdrawal symptoms.

questions.question_text: The endocrine effects of neuroleptics would include all except?
questions.explanation: The endocrine effects include secondary amenorrhoea rather than primary.

questions.question_text: A patient with Parkinson's disease experiences visual hallucinations on levodopa/carbidopa therapy. The most appropriate intervention would be to initiate treatment with which of the following medications?
questions.explanation: Quetiapine is an atypical antipsychotic with a reduced likelihood of causing drug-induced parkinsonism.

questions.question_text: Poor response to lithium prophylaxis is predicted by?

options.text: family loading of bipolar spectrum disorders

questions.explanation: Patients with rapid cycling are less likely to respond to lithium treatment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor?
questions.explanation: Reboxetine is the first selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor used in depression treatment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following has no evidence-based support when prescribing antidementia drug donepezil?

options.text: Reduces the progression of cognitive decline
Improves the amount of daily activities in some patients

questions.explanation: There is conflicting evidence on the long-term benefits of donepezil, particularly regarding time to institutionalization.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following has high D2/high 5HT2 activity?
questions.explanation: Risperidone is characterized by high D2 and high 5HT2 activity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following groups of medications are associated with bruxism more often than the others listed?
questions.explanation: Teeth grinding in children (bruxism) is associated with the use of stimulants for ADHD treatment.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a pure D2 antagonist?
questions.explanation: Sulpiride is a pure D2 antagonist, while Amisulpride is a D2/D3 antagonist.

questions.question_text: Which of the following increases the risk of withdrawal reactions to therapeutic drugs?

options.text: Having multiple active metabolites with slow clearance
Drugs being a partial agonist instead of full agonist

questions.explanation: Anticholinergic properties can lead to cholinergic rebound symptoms upon withdrawal.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs is not suitable for treating acute mania?
questions.explanation: Topiramate has not been supported by rigorous trials for treating acute mania.

questions.question_text: Receptor blockade in which dopaminergic pathway results in increased prolactin levels in the body?
questions.explanation: Blockade of dopamine­2 receptors in the tuberoinfundibular pathway leads to increased prolactin levels.

questions.question_text: Drug X produces improvement in depression when given at a dose of 10mg. Drug Y which acts via the same mechanism as X produces the same improvement when given at a dose of 20mg. When X and Y are given together, Y binds to more receptors in a quicker and stronger fashion than X. Which of the following is true?

options.text: X and Y have equal affinity but different potency
X and Y have equal potency but different affinity
X and Y are equally efficacious
Y has lesser affinity then X
X is less potent than Y

correct_answer.text: X and Y are equally efficacious

correct_answers.text: X and Y are equally efficacious

questions.explanation: Efficacy refers to the maximum clinical response a drug can produce; both X and Y are equally efficacious.
